title: Three scenes: the dispatcher, the price, and the leaf

frames.title: Dispatcher.Dispatch
frames.explanation: Scene 0's root. The entry point, and the scene the walkthrough returns to at the end.

relations.note: the child node nested on this line

frames.title: ValidationHandler.Handle
frames.explanation: Nested inside Dispatch at its call site — a two-node scene.

frames.title: PricingHandler.Handle
frames.explanation: Scene 1's root. The same frame that was a nested child in the old one-scene plan is a root here — a frame's place is a property of its scene, not of the file.

frames.title: SubInvoker.Apply
frames.explanation: Scene 2 is one frame: a single file, shown as a one-node tree. This is the shape every 'explain this method' plan now takes.

steps.ttsText: Dispatch takes one order, throws on null, and empties the failure list it is about to fill.

steps.explanation: Three handlers, one of them nested here
steps.note: Only validation is a node in this scene. The other two handlers get their own scene.
steps.ttsText: Then three handlers run in a fixed order. This scene keeps only the first of them on screen, because a scene is what the reader is looking at rather than everything the plan will ever mention.
Validation counts what it inspected and starts a list of problems, one string per thing wrong with the order.
It returns a clean verdict when the problem list is empty, and a rejected one carrying the problems when it is not.

steps.note: Scene change: the two nodes of scene 0 are gone and two different ones are up.
steps.example: verdict rejected → Money.Zero, and nothing below this line runs
steps.ttsText: Now the pricing handler. Notice that the previous two files are no longer on screen: this step is in another scene, so the whole tree was replaced rather than added to.
It takes the order subtotal and hands it to the invoker, with the scale factor and the shared options.
The invoker validates the factor, counts the invocation, and normalises the amount before deciding whether it is worth settling.

steps.note: A one-frame scene. This is what 'Explain This (Audio)' on a single method now looks like.
steps.ttsText: The leaf. Every enabled adjustment runs over the amount in registration order, and each one is recorded before the next runs.
Then it guards against a negative total and rounds to the configured precision, returning the amount unchanged when it is already rounded.

steps.explanation: Back in scene 0 — rebuilt, not restored
steps.note: The scene is built fresh. Any node you collapsed or resized in it earlier is back at its default.
steps.ttsText: And back to Dispatch to finish: if the verdict was not acceptable, its problems become the dispatcher's failures. Scene zero is built again from scratch, because the tree holds one scene at a time.
